messages.body: Task 3 of 8 (fixcheck.py check --enforce) halted after the protocol's full 5-attempt ladder: ledger line 'T3: halt review=5 reason=ladder-end' in .dev/tasks/to-do/TASK-WF-spec-20261108-181543/progress.md. Tasks 1-2 are complete; Tasks 4-8 (skill page, variant command, sync, experiment build, INSTALL.md and briefs) are not started. State: 79 tests pass; all 6 earlier blocking findings are fixed; 26,000 fuzz cases pass. The last review found 2 open blocking defects, both edge cases: F5.1, when a reviser inserts an UNDECLARED code fence in the middle of the text next to an in-budget fix, --enforce can either exit 1 or (worse, silently) write a sentence twice (6 of 2,142 adversarial pairwise probes); F5.2, the diff_hunks docstring overclaims: an undeclared join of two table rows or two paragraphs is not detected as a change. Options: A = stop now and report failed with the halt record (what my brief says by default; nothing after Task 3 is built). B = you accept Task 3 as it stands (a Ruling naming F5.1 and F5.2 as known open defects, listed in INSTALL.md), and I continue with Tasks 4-8. C = operator fix path of the protocol: I fix F5.1 and F5.2 now, then one fresh operator review; if it passes, Task 3 completes and I continue with Tasks 4-8; if it fails, Task 3 halts again and I stop as in A. Recommendation: C, because both defects are understood and narrow, and the deliverables after Task 3 need this script; if you prefer certainty over completeness, A.
